item.title: F1 Heads to Austin for Crucial United States Grand Prix
item.description: Photo by: David Kirouac Formula 1 heads to Austin, Texas, this weekend for the United States Grand Prix as the 2026 championship battle continues to heat up. With the season entering its final stretch, every point becomes increasingly important as the drivers prepare for one of the most challenging circuits on the calendar. The race takes place at Circuit of the Americas, a track known for its combination of high-speed corners, technical sections and strong overtaking opportunities. The 56-lap event will test both driver skill and car performance, making strategy and qualifying position important factors heading into Sunday. Antonelli Leads the Championship Battle Kimi Antonelli enters the weekend as the championship leader after an impressive season with Mercedes. The young Italian has established himself as a major contender, but the pressure will continue to increase as the remaining races approach. His teammate George Russell will also be looking to challenge for the victory and close the gap in the standings. Mercedes has shown strong pace throughout the season, giving both drivers an opportunity to fight near the front. Max Verstappen is another driver to watch. The Red Bull star recently won the Singapore Grand Prix, strengthening his momentum heading into Austin. Although the championship picture remains challenging, Verstappen has demonstrated that he can still compete for race victories. Ferrari will also hope to remain in contention, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton looking to capitalize on any opportunities that emerge during the weekend. Circuit of the Americas Could Deliver Exciting Racing Circuit of the Americas has become one of Formula 1’s most recognizable venues since joining the calendar in 2012. Its uphill run into Turn 1 provides an excellent overtaking opportunity, while the fast opening sequence and technical final sector challenge drivers throughout the lap. Teams will also need to pay close attention to tire management and race strategy. With several long corners placing significant loads on the tires, finding the right balance between speed and durability could make a difference late in the race. Practice and qualifying will be especially important as teams evaluate their setups before Sunday’s event. A Critical Weekend Ahead The United States Grand Prix offers another opportunity for championship contenders to gain valuable points before the series travels to Mexico. With Antonelli leading the standings, Verstappen carrying momentum and Mercedes facing competition from Ferrari and the rest of the field, Austin could produce another major storyline in an increasingly important stage of the season. The green flag waves Sunday, October 25, with the race scheduled for 3 p.m. local time in Austin.

item.title: Liverpool make approach for World Cup midfielder
item.description: Liverpool make approach for World Cup midfielder Liverpool have made an approach for a World Cup star. The Reds are aiming to bring in a midfielder when they can. There's no question that Liverpool want a new midfielder. And as they should do - there's currently a massive whole in the middle of the pitch and teams are finding it far too easy to attack it. We saw that in an otherwise good performance against Villarreal this week. Really, though, we've seen it again and again this season and the plan right now is for Trey Nyoni to plug it. Nyoni, however, is an inexperienced teenager and banking on him to solidify your elite UEFA Champions League team is a risk probably not worth taking just yet. That has Liverpool looking at the transfer market - and they're already making moves. Liverpool make an approach for Felix Nmecha Sky Sports Germany claims that Liverpool have made an approach to the entourage of Felix Nmecha. This is typically the first port of call before making a move for a player - they're trying to find out how realistic a move is. Nmecha is undoubtedly one of the most interesting midfield players in Europe. He's tall, strong, powerful and loves running with the ball - a modern midfielder who looks to win his one-on-one matchups. The report is keen to stress that Liverpool do have other options in mind and that this certainly isn't a case of them going all-in on Nmecha. It appears he's on the shortlist, though, and could well end up being the pick if any deal for him looks better than deals elsewhere. All we can say with confidence is that Liverpool want a midfielder and that they're looking at an expensive category of player. The kind who can slot right into the mix with the current group - and possibly from January. Because that's the other side of this. Liverpool don't just want to know if a move is possible. They want to know when as signing the right player in January could ultimately transform their season ahead of the push for trophies. And Nmecha may well be that player.

item.title: IndyCar Unveils 2027 Schedule Featuring Historic Barcelona Race
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez The NTT IndyCar Series has officially revealed its complete 2027 schedule, featuring 17 races, several familiar stops and a major international addition that will take the series back to Europe for the first time in two decades. The biggest announcement is the addition of Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain, which will host IndyCar on July 18, 2027. The race marks a significant moment for the series as it continues looking for ways to expand its audience and bring American open-wheel racing to new fans around the world. The 2027 season will begin on March 7 with the traditional trip to the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida. IndyCar will then head to Phoenix Raceway on March 13 before visiting Arlington, Texas, on March 21, giving the series three consecutive weekends of racing to open the year. The early portion of the schedule also includes Barber Motorsports Park, Long Beach and the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course before the biggest event of the season. Indianapolis 500 Remains the Highlight The 111th running of the Indianapolis 500 is scheduled for May 30, once again serving as the centerpiece of the IndyCar calendar. The historic race remains one of the biggest events in motorsports and a major opportunity for drivers to establish themselves in the championship picture. Following the Indy 500, the series will visit Detroit on June 6 before heading to World Wide Technology Raceway, Road America and Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course. The summer schedule then features the Barcelona race, followed by Portland International Raceway on August 1 and the Streets of Markham in Ontario, Canada, on August 15. Nashville and Washington, D.C. Leave the Schedule The new schedule also brings some notable changes. IndyCar will not return to Nashville Superspeedway in 2027, while the Washington, D.C., Freedom 250 Grand Prix remains a one-time event rather than becoming a permanent stop. The series will instead feature a doubleheader at the historic Milwaukee Mile on August 28-29, giving teams two opportunities to earn valuable championship points during one weekend. The season finale is scheduled for September 5 at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in California. Another important detail is that every IndyCar race will once again air on FOX in the United States. With a mix of ovals, road courses, street circuits and an international destination, the 2027 schedule offers a diverse challenge for drivers competing for the championship.

item.title: Brewers Add 2 Time All-Star Starting Pitcher To World Series Roster – Breaking News
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are adding a familiar name to their pitching staff for the World Series. Brandon Woodruff has officially been added to Milwaukee’s 26-man roster for the Fall Classic against the Tampa Bay Rays, giving the Brewers another experienced arm as they pursue the first World Series championship in franchise history. Woodruff takes the roster spot of right-hander Chad Patrick, marking the only change Milwaukee made to its roster ahead of Game 1 on Friday. The move gives the two-time All-Star an opportunity to pitch in the World Series after spending months working his way back from a shoulder injury. Also Read: Milwaukee Brewers Name Starting Pitcher For Game 1 Of The World Series Sep 6, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Brandon Woodruff (53) delivers a pitch against the Pittsburgh Pirates during the first inning at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Brewers’ Brandon Woodruff Returns for the World Series Woodruff has not pitched in a game since July 4, when he made a start against the Arizona Diamondbacks. A shoulder injury initially appeared likely to end his season, and he was expected to undergo surgery in August. However, Woodruff’s recovery took a different turn when the procedure was no longer considered necessary. He resumed throwing and gradually worked his way back onto the mound, keeping alive the possibility of returning during the postseason. The final step came earlier this week, when Woodruff faced live hitters during a batting practice session. His performance gave the Brewers another reason to consider including him on the World Series roster. Milwaukee ultimately decided the potential benefit was worth the risk. Woodruff is a veteran who has spent his entire major league career with the Brewers, and the team believes his experience could be valuable against Tampa Bay. Woodruff’s Numbers With the Brewers in 2026 Despite his injury-shortened season, Woodruff was effective when available. He finished the regular season with a 2-2 record and a 2.98 ERA across nine starts. The 33-year-old right-hander has been one of Milwaukee’s most dependable pitchers over the years. Since making his major league debut in 2017, he has compiled a 55-30 record with a 3.10 ERA. That experience is particularly important in October. Woodruff has appeared in eight career postseason games, recording a 3.18 ERA and 40 strikeouts in those appearances. Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold acknowledged that there are uncertainties surrounding Woodruff’s return, but made it clear the pitcher was worth considering. “This is a guy that’s one of the most successful, dominant big-game pitchers I’ve ever been around,” Arnold said . “A lot of unknowns there, but obviously, the good version of that guy is somebody you’d love to have on your roster.” What Woodruff’s Addition Means for Milwaukee Aug 8, 2025; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Brandon Wood

item.title: Roger Goodell identifies Tokyo as NFL’s next target for international game
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect On the second day of the 2026 NFL season, the league hosted its first-ever game in Melbourne, Australia, between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. On game day, CNBC’s Alex Sherman published an interview with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who emphasized global expansion as a top priority. Since then, the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys played the first-ever NFL game in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and the past three weeks of NFL slates have featured a game in London. This Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game (sensing a theme?) in Paris. Ahead of that game, Goodell joined NFL Daily with Gregg Rosenthal to discuss the NFL’s growing global imprint and hinted at the next. Rosenthal asked Goodell about the importance of international media and TV rights . “Well, they’re all important, whether it’s your partnerships in the media or sponsorships or, frankly, playing the games,” Goodell said. “But they all have to be coordinated. They all have to work together. Ultimately, even in the States, the media partners are the ones who give you the greatest access to the fans.” “Media partnerships are really critical to us, and we look for the best media partners—as many as we can—and have that global reach,” Goodell added. Goodell maintained the company line, as expected from the commissioner, but he did name the next city the NFL’s eyeing. “Tokyo is clearly on our list,” Goodell said. “Whether it’s next year or the year after, it’s coming at some point in the near future.” As for why the NFL is so emboldened in expanding globally, Goodell said, “Australia was off the charts. On a Friday morning at 10:30, having 100,000 people in the stadium was an incredible experience for us. I think it’s opened up new opportunities for us. “The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. item.title: Bournemouth has already closed the January door for Arsenal target
item.description: Bournemouth has already closed the January door for Arsenal target Eli Junior Kroupi was the highest-scoring teenager in the Premier League last season, and many expected him to leave Bournemouth at the end of the campaign, with Arsenal among the clubs interested in securing his signature. The Frenchman enjoyed an impressive season, establishing himself as a dangerous attacking player and making a significant contribution to the Cherries’ success. His goals proved difficult for opponents to contain, helping Bournemouth secure qualification for the Europa League. His performances attracted attention from several clubs, with Arsenal among those monitoring his progress and considering whether he could strengthen their attacking options. However, Kroupi suffered an injury during pre-season and has yet to regain sufficient fitness to start matches for Bournemouth. Although his return is expected soon, his absence has temporarily limited his opportunities to continue building on the progress he made last season. Arsenal have nevertheless maintained their interest in the young forward . Arsenal consider Kroupi as a striker option The Gunners could look to offload Viktor Gyokeres in January, creating a potential need to recruit another striker to replace the Swedish international. Kroupi has emerged as one of the players they are interested in, given his performances last season and his potential to develop further. Arsenal will be keen to assess his progress once he returns to action, particularly as they consider their options for strengthening the squad . The Frenchman is reportedly open to making the move, while other interested clubs are also waiting to see him return to the pitch and rediscover his goalscoring form. His age and previous performances could make him an appealing option for a club looking to invest in a young forward. However, Arsenal may have to reconsider the timing of any potential approach if they want to bring him to the Emirates Stadium. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images) Bournemouth resist a January departure According to Standard Sport , Bournemouth have no intention of allowing Kroupi to leave before the end of this season and have already ruled out a departure during the January transfer window. The Cherries want to retain the forward because they expect him to contribute to their efforts during the current campaign. Allowing him to leave midway through the season would mean losing a player they hope can make an impact once he returns to full fitness. That stance presents a significant obstacle for Arsenal, even if their interest remains strong and Kroupi is willing to consider a transfer. item.title: Kaio Jorge: ‘Without the injury I’d still be at Juventus, I’d do much better now’
item.description: Kaio Jorge: ‘Without the injury I’d still be at Juventus, I’d do much better now’ Former Juventus striker Kaio Jorge believes he would still be at the club if not for the serious injury that wrecked his time in Turin, and says he is ready to return to Italy. According to EuropaCalcio , the Brazilian spoke to Cronache di Spogliatoio about his spell with the Bianconeri, which was cut short when he ruptured the patellar tendon in his right knee playing for the Under-23s in February 2022. “In five months at Juve I played less than I expected. I hoped to get at least 20 minutes a game, because I was always training at my best during the week and scoring in friendlies,” he said. “The injury definitely affected my path in Turin.” Juventus forward Kaio Jorge reacts after a goal opportunity during the Italian Serie A football match between Juventus and Sassuolo on October 27, 2021 at the Allianz Stadium in Turin. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) (Photo by MARCO BERTORELLO/AFP via Getty Images) Kaio Jorge ready for Serie A return after failed Juventus spell Kaio Jorge joined Juventus from Santos as a 19-year-old in 2021. After a long recovery and a loan spell at Frosinone in 2023-24, he joined Cruzeiro permanently in June 2024 and has rebuilt his career in Brazil. “I remain very attached to the club, which helped me through the difficult period of the injury and believed in me, allowing me to realise my dream of playing in Europe,” he explained. “Now I’d be ready to come back to Italy, maybe even to Juve. Today I’d do much better.” His comments come at an awkward time for Luciano Spalletti, who has 16 players injured and is short of options in attack. Juventus are expected to look for a striker in January, although there is no sign yet of a move.

Penske Transportation Solutions, the leasing, rental and logistics side, reports more than $13 billion in annual revenue and a fleet of more than 370,000 vehicles. Since 2018, Hitachi Digital Services and GlobalLogic, a Hitachi Group company, have worked as an extension of Penske’s engineering organization on that side of the business. Racing sponsors rarely publish return-on-investment numbers. This one did: more than $18 million in annualized savings from faster diagnostics and predictive maintenance, more than 90,000 breakdowns prevented, and roughly 15 minutes saved on each repair. The work covers AI-assisted guided repair, a modernized rental platform, procurement tools, generative AI that makes millions of contracts and vendor records searchable, and an “agentic AI” platform still in development. If that sounds familiar to a race engineer, it should. Every IndyCar team already runs this way: life every part, trend the sensor data, and pull a component before it fails rather than after. Hitachi’s argument is that the same discipline, applied to a rental truck in a depot instead of an upright on a Dallara, is worth eight figures a year. Seen that way, the front wing is the trade-show booth and the fleet contract is the sale. That’s a big part of why this deal has lasted longer than plenty of flashier liveries. Why the front wing works for this kind of sponsor Front-wing placement is associate-level real estate, but it has one big advantage over a primary livery: it appears on all three cars every weekend, whoever’s name is on the car. In 2026, the car names were Astemo on the No. 2, DEX on the No. 3 and Verizon on the No. 12. Hitachi was on the endplates of all three, and those endplates sit at the very front of every head-on photo and every onboard shot from the car behind. There’s also a neat bit of timing. Hitachi’s Penske run started in 2012, the same season the current Dallara chassis entered service. IndyCar’s series notebook says the extension covers 2027, which is that chassis’ final season. The IR-28, unveiled in July, debuts in 2028 with new front and rear wings, a more aggressive road-and-street configuration and a design meant to cut outwash. When the wing changes shape, sponsor placement gets renegotiated whether anyone plans for it or not. What the logo has been along for Team Penske’s 2024 release credited the Hitachi car with 15 IndyCar wins as a primary sponsor, starting with Helio Castroneves at Detroit in 2014, along with Indianapolis 500 wins and five series championships across the life of the partnership. Alex Palou won the championship with 631 points and six wins. David Malukas, in his first year in the No. 12, was Penske’s best finisher in fifth with 514 points and no wins. All three were inside a midfield where the gap from second to fifth was just 31 points . The off-track context matters too. A partner from before that upheaval re-signing during the team’s 60th-anniversary season is worth more than a press-release adjective. Jonathan Diuguid, Team Penske’s IndyCar president, called Hitachi “a critical partner across the Penske organization,” and the fleet numbers show he meant the whole organization, not only the race shop. It may well continue, since supplier relationships in IndyCar often cross brand lines, but it’s the question this announcement left unanswered. Whether Hitachi follows the wing into 2028. A new car means new surfaces, new sponsor maps and new pricing. Paddock deals tied to the IR-28 will start showing up over the coming year, and Chevrolet’s own team commitments are already moving, as Arrow McLaren’s re-signing for the 2.4-liter era showed. Penske’s three-car balance. Malukas outscoring both of his champion teammates in year one is the most interesting competitive storyline Penske carries into the winter. The sponsor is staying put. item.title: Gladbah earn first points with comeback win at underwhelming Stuttgart
item.description: Gladbah earn first points with comeback win at underwhelming Stuttgart Borussia Mönchengladbach avoided becoming the first team to start a Bundesliga season with seven defeats as they beat Champions League participants Stuttgart away from home in a five-goal thriller. Sebastian Hoeneß started Dženan Pejčinović and Ermedin Demirović together for the first time since the defeat in Hoffenheim, and that decision bore fruit inside the first five minutes. The Germany U21 international provided the assist for the quickfire volley by the makeshift captain. Moritz Nicolas should've done much better in Gladbach's goal as he had the chance to parry the ball. With Deniz Undav starting on the bench, the combination of the two strikers created another decent scoring opportunity ten minutes later. However, the visitors started to dominate proceedings from the half-hour mark. Shuto Machino and Fabio Chiarodia failed to test Dennis Seimen from promising positions before Joe Scally stunned Stuttgart with his second goal from as many away games. On his home debut, the young goalkeeper was unable to react fast as the US defender guided Zento Uno's effort into the net with a clever backheel. Gladbach lost all of their six league games since the start of the season, but they should've taken a lead before the half-time break. Seimen denied Florian Neuhaus before the the woodwork came to the rescue of the hosts from Wael Mohya's attempt in the last couple of actions in injury-time. The trend continued after the break as Mohya wrestled Leo Sauer and Lorenz Assignon before finding the unmarked Machino, who put Gladbach ahead for the first time with a powerful hit. Hoeneß wastes no time in making triple changes as Undav, Bilal El Khannouss and Jamie Leweling. The hosts tried to respond quickly, but the cellar-dwellers doubled their advantage after yet another scramble around Stuttgart's box. The magnificent Mahoya scored for the second week running with a close range header from Scally's pinpoint delivery. Seimen was at fault as he was unable to deal with Mahoya's weak effort that led to a second chance for the 17-year-old midfielder. Stuttgart continued to push to get back in the game, but they were unable to beat Nicolas until Demirović's header halved the deficit in the 83rd minute. The Bosnian striker’s second strike of the night was the 22nd goal Gladbach conceded this season. After his mistake that led to the opening goal of the game, Nicolas had a strong second-half performance, including his 90th minute save to deny El Khannouss. Alexander Blessin celebrated the huge win with his players after they defended weathered several crosses into the box in injury-time. Gladbach will host Karlsruhe in the midweek cup action, while Stuttgart travel to Paderborn for the second time this month.

item.title: Canucks’ Brock Boeser sends blunt warning after ninth straight loss for Vancouver
item.description: Brock Boeser did not hide his frustration after the Vancouver Canucks suffered their ninth consecutive loss. Vancouver fell 5-2 to the Detroit Red Wings on Thursday, leaving the NHL veteran winger questioning the team’s structure, communication, and commitment to its playing style. “It’s the same stuff game after game,” Boeser told reporters. “I don’t know where the disconnect is, if guys in here aren’t listening to what the coaches are preaching on our style of play, or some of our structure’s not working, or what it is, but it’s embarrassing.” MORE: Leon Draisaitl praises Connor McDavid’s evolution after Oilers star breaks Wayne Gretzky’s record The defeat dropped Vancouver to 2-9-1, extending a difficult start to the season. Lucas Raymond scored twice and added an assist for Detroit, while Vancouver struggled defensively from the opening minutes. The Red Wings scored three times in the first nine minutes, putting the Canucks under immediate pressure. Kevin Lankinen finished with 26 saves, but Vancouver could not recover from the early deficit. Brock Boeser questions Canucks’ team structure Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Detroit Red Wings defenseman William Wallinder (54) celebrates near Vancouver Canucks forward Brock Boeser at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Boeser also criticized the team’s inability to operate as a connected unit for an entire game. He believes Vancouver has shown better hockey in the past but has failed to reproduce that standard consistently. “We are a way better hockey team than we’re playing,” Boeser said. “To consistently show up to the rink and be disconnected out there” is embarrassing, he added. The winger said the Canucks sometimes manage only one period of cohesive, five-man hockey. That inconsistency suggests the problem extends beyond individual mistakes. Vancouver’s defensive struggles require more than a short-term scoring boost. The coaching staff must establish clearer defensive responsibilities and improve communication across all four lines. Boeser also pointed to the team’s lack of offensive pressure, saying Vancouver was not generating enough shots. Without sustained possession, the Canucks leave their defense under constant pressure. “So something’s not working, and I don’t know if guys don’t listen or, like I said, structure, something in the structure we need to fix or what it is, but we definitely have a lot better in this room,” Boeser said. item.title: What to know about the Racing Sausages, Milwaukee Brewers' most famous mascots
item.description: For more than 30 years, a collection of 7-foot-tall sausages have entertained Milwaukee Brewers fans at the bottom of the sixth inning with a foot race. The Famous Racing Sausages, some of Brew City's most identifiable mascots, burst onto the field in 1993 and have been serving up photo finishes, triumphant moments and even a few controversies ever since. The racing sausages were an innovation for Major League Baseball and gave rise to live-action mascot races elsewhere, like the racing presidents in Washington, DC and the racing pierogies in Pittsburgh. When they debuted Back in 1992, the sausages were simply animated, cartoon links on the jumbotron at the old County Stadium. Michael Dillon, a local graphic designer, worked with the Brewers to take the sausages off the screen and onto the field. He designed and created the costumes, and the original trio debuted in 1993. Their first appearance was a surprise to almost everyone in the ballpark, including the umpire and the players. The sausages appeared as animations on screen, then the feed cut out and they came running out of the left-field corner of County Stadium. What's changed over the years Hot Dog joined the race in 1997. Then Chorizo debuted in 2006 and became a fixture of the lineup a year later. Quinn Hughes was on Team USA when they won a gold medal last winter too, and his brother Jack is now teammates in New Jersey with Hellebuyck. So… what does today’s trade mean for the Minnesota Wild, and their still unaccomplished missions to sign Quinn Hughes and trade for Dylan Larkin? Well, there are multiple NHL insiders weighing into that conversation this afternoon, including If the Devils are serious about reuniting the three Hughes brothers over the next year, whether via trade or free agency, Mehta made the ultimate chess move. As of now, after checking in again this week, Hughes remains undecided on his future. He hasn’t told the Wild he won’t extend. However, he also hasn’t told them he will. He’s undecided, period. But let me say this if I can venture to guess the many thoughts that are dancing around in the superstar defenseman’s head: “Do I stay in Minnesota where the Wild are a legit Stanley Cup contender or fulfill our family dream of playing with Jack and Luke in New Jersey even if the Devils don’t yet look like a true … wait, they just got Hellebuyck? While he did mention how this deal could affect the Wild in a negative way, like LeBrun above, Russo seems more intrigued by how Winnipeg’s modest return for Hellebuyck might push Red Wings’ GM Shawn Horcoff to take what Guerin has on the table for Larkin now, before the package shrinks. Could Hellebuyck trade help MN Wild in Larkin trade talks? Minnesota’s top hockey insider even went as far as to say that he can “almost guarantee” that Minnesota’s offer for Larkin includes one good young player, a couple of other rostered players and multiple first round picks. Winnipeg didn’t even get one first in their deal for Hellebuyck. One wonders if this return for an award-winning, gold medal-winning Hellebuyck gets Detroit Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff’s attention because I can almost guarantee you the Wild have offered a good young player, one or two other roster players that make decent money and multiple first-round picks for Dylan Larkin . Remember, while Horcoff may not be intrigued with the positioning of where those picks could end up if the Wild are good (late first-round picks if the Wild get to where they hope), Horcoff can always use those futures in subsequent trades. Plus, if the roster players are pending UFAs, those players can be flipped at the deadline. Michael Russo – The Athletic Related: Wild Insider Agrees: Dylan Larkin Trade Feels Imminent Larkin is coming off a 34-goal, 67-point season in 74 games, and he has five points in eight games this year. He also carries an $8.7 million cap hit, which the MN Wild could clear by placing Brock Faber on long-term injured reserve, if they don’t make the money work directly in the trade. Faber has not played this season after having surgery for a skull fracture. LTIR requires a player to miss at least 10 games and 24 days of the regular season, and Faber has already missed all 11 of Minnesota’s games. Either way, Russo agrees with his colleague. This deal certainly puts more pressure on Guerin to get the Larkin deal done. What I do think is this certainly puts more pressure on the Wild to execute this Larkin trade, and one wonders now if the Wild’s offer becomes more intriguing for Horcoff. Michael Russo – The Athletic Why the Devils trade matters for Quinn Hughes The other worry for Wild fans is how the Connor Hellebuyck deal might affect contract negotiations with Quinn Hughes, who is in the final year of his deal, which currently carries a $7.85 million cap hit. It’s widely known that Hughes is due to become an unrestricted free agent next July, and that he eventually wants to play with his brother brothers, Jack and Luke. Both currently play in New Jersey with Hellebuyck. Russo wrote that Hughes “loves Hellebuyck,” and that a stronger Devils team “absolutely gets [Hughes] attention.” Like Minnesota, New Jersey’s money situation ($16.8 million in projected cap space next season) would make signing another Hughes brother for $20 million difficult. Obviously, the Wild’s best bet is to land Hughes’ best friend, Dylan Larkin. Russo still believes that would entice Hughes to re-sign as soon as possible. For that, Guerin will need a Red Wings front office that’s actually willing to play ball… Read more at Minnesota Sports Fan

OKLAHOMA CITY — After the Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the San Antoino Spurs on Tuesday , head coach Mark Daigneault watched his team overcome a poor shooting performance to top the Denver Nuggets 96-84 in their home opener at the Paycom Center. From limiting one All-Star center in Victor Wembanyama, the Thunder contained Nuggets All-Star center Nikola Jokic , before erasing a nine-point deficit to cruise to a double-digit victory. For Daigneault, the Thunder’s defense limiting Jamal Murray (six points, 2-for-11) and Jokic (13 points, 5-of-19) to a combined 19 points on 7-for-30 shooting made all the difference despite shooting below 40% from the field, and 25.6% from deep. “For us, that was a game plan in terms of execution, I thought the job we did on Jokic and Murray, specifically, is what won us the game,” Daigneault said. “They missed some shots that they can make, obviously, but we made them earn everything. It was about clean of a game plan execution you can have, especially this early in the season. And I just thought the guys did a great job on a night where we didn’t shoot it great, and it was a muddy game. We didn’t get out of character at any point. That’s a really positive way to win a game.” Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault praised his team for sticking with the defensive schemes that would eventually catapault his team’s offense. The Nuggets shot at a 37.9% clip against Oklahoma City, including 26.7% from beyond the 3-point arc. “There can be nights where the shot isn’t falling and you can just talk yourself into it not being your night. And this team is too competitive to do that most night,” Daigneault said. “We don’t look for excuses. We look for solutions. That’s where the energy, the defense, the toughness [comes from]. It wasn’t Denver’s night either. They missed some shots. “There’s always a shot variance to it. But it was a muddy game and I just thought we worked the game, stuck with the game, and it was our energy and our defense, and our toughness that prevailed tonight. And that’s a good sign. It’s a good way to win a game.” Jalen Williams led with a game-high 21 points, five rebounds, and three assists. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 17 points on a dreadful 6-for-19 shooting, including 3-for-11 from deep, and Chet Holmgren dominated the glass, pulling down 17 rebounds to go with his 12 points, and four blocks. The Thunder (2-0) will host the LA Clippers at the Paycom Center on Sunday. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
